**Severity:** High (availability). **Confidence:** High for missing aggregate bound; OOM not reproduced.
This is a source-flow finding, not a runtime reproduction. No exploit inputs, destructive tests, or application changes were made.

## Root cause and evidence
[crates/docbin/src/notes.rs:10–25](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/docbin/src/notes.rs#L10-L25) accepts individually increasing ranges without checking monotonicity/non-overlap across the note PLC. [crates/docbin/src/lib.rs:199–214](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/docbin/src/lib.rs#L199-L214) walks and materializes each accepted range independently. Source-character and part-count caps do not bound aggregate decoded story content.

## Conditions and realistic impact
Malformed note tables can repeatedly reference overlapping large footnote/endnote ranges. A bounded source story becomes many owned output stories, multiplying CPU/memory consumption. This is a static resource-budget finding, not a demonstrated crash or exploit.

## Recommended remediation
Validate PLC order and non-overlap and enforce one shared decoded-character/object/work budget across all stories before materialization.

## Suggested regression tests
Public DOC import with small injected budgets and overlapping/nonmonotonic note ranges; assert deterministic limit/error results and bounded aggregate work. Include a valid nonoverlapping control.

title: Rendering/PDF: image limits are applied after allocation and raster budgets allow excessive memory
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Scope and verification
Read-only source audit of upstream main at 159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0 (rechecked against upstream before filing). Audit reference: **H7**.

**Severity:** High (availability). **Confidence:** High for allocation paths; exhaustion not reproduced.
This is a source-flow finding, not a runtime reproduction. No exploit inputs, destructive tests, or application changes were made.

## Root cause and evidence
[crates/render/src/lib.rs:170–195](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/render/src/lib.rs#L170-L195) decodes and converts to RGBA before checking dimensions and then makes a premultiplied copy. [crates/pdf/src/lib.rs:1486–1496](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/pdf/src/lib.rs#L1486-L1496) checks dimensions after decoding. [crates/render/src/lib.rs:402–425](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/render/src/lib.rs#L402-L425) allows a 16,000×16,000 output, whose pixel vector alone is 1,024,000,000 bytes, before renderer/encoding copies.

## Conditions and realistic impact
Large low-channel-count images or large page raster requests can cause severe memory pressure. image 0.25.10 has a default decoded-output budget (512 MiB), so initial decode is not unbounded; conversion/copy/output allocations still escape that budget.

## Recommended remediation
Configure dimensions/allocation limits before decoding; add checked total-pixel and conversion-byte budgets, aggregate per-operation media limits, and practical output raster limits returning explicit errors.

## Suggested regression tests
Budget boundaries for low-channel-to-RGBA conversion, cache-rejected images, repeated images, page rendering and PNG encoding. Use small limits rather than memory-exhaustion tests.

title: DOCX: header/footer references reset recursion depth across distinct parts
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Scope and verification
Read-only source audit of upstream main at 159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0 (rechecked against upstream before filing). Audit reference: **H8**.

**Severity:** High potential availability impact. **Confidence:** High for recursion gap; stack exhaustion remains unverified.
This is a source-flow finding, not a runtime reproduction. No exploit inputs, destructive tests, or application changes were made.

## Root cause and evidence
[crates/docx/src/read/story.rs:376–417](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/docx/src/read/story.rs#L376-L417) follows section/header references while parsing paragraphs. [crates/docx/src/read/mod.rs:622–640](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/docx/src/read/mod.rs#L622-L640) reserves an ID but then creates a fresh StoryCtx and calls read_blocks with depth 0. Memoization prevents cycles, not long chains of distinct parts.

## Conditions and realistic impact
Malformed packages with a long distinct-part reference chain grow the Rust stack despite per-part XML depth limits. ZIP/part-count caps are much larger than a safe active recursion bound. No runtime failure threshold or exploit payload is claimed.

## Recommended remediation
Load referenced stories iteratively or carry a shared low active cross-part recursion/work budget and return a clear limit error.

## Suggested regression tests
Public DOCX read tests for distinct chains and self/multi-part cycles under a small budget. The chain should fail deterministically without recursive stack growth.

title: Zotero bridge edits bypass document protection and tracked-change enforcement
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Scope and verification
Read-only source audit of upstream main at 159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0 (rechecked against upstream before filing). Audit reference: **H9**.

**Severity:** High (application editing integrity). **Confidence:** High; source confirmed.
This is a source-flow finding, not a runtime reproduction. No exploit inputs, destructive tests, or application changes were made.

## Root cause and evidence
[crates/zotero/src/bridge.rs:184–195](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/zotero/src/bridge.rs#L184-L195) dispatches directly against Session. [crates/zotero/src/bridge.rs:244–252](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/zotero/src/bridge.rs#L244-L252) inserts text and [crates/zotero/src/bridge.rs:402–422](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/zotero/src/bridge.rs#L402-L422) replaces field text directly in Document, bypassing Session::run protection/exception-region checks and revision-aware edits.

## Conditions and realistic impact
Zotero insertion, refresh, code removal, or conversion on a protected document, outside editable exceptions, or inside locked content can make changes ordinary commands refuse. Tracked-changes-only edits need not become rejectable revisions. This concerns application editing restrictions, not cryptographic access control.

## Recommended remediation
Use a shared engine transaction/protection/control-lock/revision interface for bridge mutations rather than direct unguarded model edits.

## Suggested regression tests
Real bridge calls under read-only, editable-region, tracked-changes-only and content-control restrictions; assert refusal with unchanged content or correct rejectable revisions.

title: MCP bridge retries mutations after ambiguous delivery, allowing duplicate execution
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Scope and verification
Read-only source audit of upstream main at 159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0. Audit reference: **H10**.
**Severity:** High (integrity). **Confidence:** high in the cited source flow. No runtime reproduction, exploit input, destructive testing, or source changes; resource-exhaustion consequences have not been measured.

## Root cause and evidence
[crates/mcp/src/backend.rs:144–183](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/mcp/src/backend.rs#L144-L183) reconnects and resends the request after round-trip I/O errors regardless of method. [apps/wordcraft/src/control_server.rs:210–245](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/apps/wordcraft/src/control_server.rs#L210-L245) has no server-side deduplication; request IDs correlate responses only.

## Conditions and realistic impact
If the app executes a mutation but its response is lost, the bridge can execute it again. Inserts and other non-idempotent edits can duplicate; filesystem effects can repeat. A successful write to the socket does not establish whether the operation executed.

## Recommended remediation
Do not replay an ambiguously delivered mutation without server-side idempotency/deduplication. Distinguish definitely-not-sent from outcome-unknown and retry only under a documented contract.

## Suggested regression tests
A controlled local transport executes an edit then drops its reply. Assert exactly-once execution or an explicit unknown-outcome error; include a safe connection-failure-before-send control.

title: Table deletion, Change Case and field unlink bypass revision and content-control checks
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Scope and verification
Read-only source audit of upstream main at 159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0. Audit reference: **M2**.
**Severity:** Medium (integrity). **Confidence:** high in the cited source flow. No runtime reproduction, exploit input, destructive testing, or source changes; resource-exhaustion consequences have not been measured.

## Root cause and evidence
[crates/engine/src/cmd/table.rs:496–546](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/engine/src/cmd/table.rs#L496-L546) physically removes table structures without tracked deletion or control-lock validation. [crates/engine/src/cmd/format.rs:414–424](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/engine/src/cmd/format.rs#L414-L424) directly changes text; [crates/engine/src/cmd/fields.rs:204–228](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/engine/src/cmd/fields.rs#L204-L228) directly replaces field markers/results. Formatting revision recording is not a general text/structural revision recorder.

## Conditions and realistic impact
With tracking enabled or locked controls in the target, these operations can alter protected content or make edits Reject All cannot restore. Ordinary Undo being available does not satisfy tracked-change or control-lock contracts.

Use centralized revision/control-aware replacement and deletion. Refuse unsupported structural edits while tracking until they have a structural revision representation.

[crates/zotero/src/bridge.rs:170–191](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/zotero/src/bridge.rs#L170-L191) checkpoints once but does not restore on error. Multi-field conversion can fail after earlier edits at [crates/zotero/src/bridge.rs:275–292](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/zotero/src/bridge.rs#L275-L292). title: Control/MCP: timeouts do not cancel queued edits and connection/framing limits are incomplete
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Scope and verification
Read-only source audit of upstream main at 159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0. Audit reference: **M4a**.
**Severity:** Medium (local availability and late mutations). **Confidence:** high in the cited source flow. No runtime reproduction, exploit input, destructive testing, or source changes; resource-exhaustion consequences have not been measured.

## Root cause and evidence
[apps/wordcraft/src/control_server.rs:240–245](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/apps/wordcraft/src/control_server.rs#L240-L245) times out the waiter after enqueueing; requests carry no execution deadline and [crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs:1580–1586](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs#L1580-L1586) executes queued requests later. [apps/wordcraft/src/control_server.rs:106–113](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/apps/wordcraft/src/control_server.rs#L106-L113) spawns one thread per accepted connection before authentication without admission limits. MCP stdio [crates/mcp/src/server.rs:64–72](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/mcp/src/server.rs#L64-L72) and remote replies [crates/mcp/src/backend.rs:144–155](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/mcp/src/backend.rs#L144-L155) use unbounded line reads; write/total-response deadlines are missing.

The app listener is loopback-only, not an Internet listener, and inbound app framing already has a 1 MiB cap.

title: Zotero transport bounds frames but not session lifetime, accumulated errors, or writes
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Scope and verification
Read-only source audit of upstream main at 159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0. Audit reference: **M4b**.
**Severity:** Medium (availability). **Confidence:** high in the cited source flow. No runtime reproduction, exploit input, destructive testing, or source changes; resource-exhaustion consequences have not been measured.

## Root cause and evidence
[crates/zotero/src/client.rs:91–125](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/zotero/src/client.rs#L91-L125) configures read timeout only, loops through frames, and appends every error. [crates/ui-egui/src/zotero.rs:96–115](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/ui-egui/src/zotero.rs#L96-L115) retains busy state and waits for callback replies without a timeout; [crates/ui-egui/src/zotero.rs:166–193](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/ui-egui/src/zotero.rs#L166-L193) retains method history until completion. The existing 32 MiB frame cap does not bound aggregate session work.

## Conditions and realistic impact
A selected local integration peer can stop reading responses, drip-feed data or continue calls/errors indefinitely. A session may stay busy indefinitely and histories can grow without bound. No unsolicited external listener exposure is asserted.

## Recommended remediation
Add write deadlines, cancellation, bounded cumulative calls/error/method history and transaction expiry. Explicitly accommodate legitimate long user-dialog waits rather than confusing per-read timeout with a session deadline.

## Suggested regression tests
Blocked write, partial-frame drip, repeated errors/calls, callback cancellation and cleanup. Use bounded fake/local peers; assert busy state eventually clears and memory accounting stays bounded.

title: File ingress reads before enforcing byte/type budgets on native and web paths

[crates/formats/src/odt.rs:1295–1302](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/formats/src/odt.rs#L1295-L1302) inflates each entry; [crates/formats/src/odt.rs:1347–1351](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/formats/src/odt.rs#L1347-L1351) checks aggregate bytes afterward, without a cache or exhausted-budget short circuit. title: Proofing repeatedly rescans whitespace tokens for every punctuation-separated word
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Scope and verification
Read-only source audit of upstream main at 159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0. Audit reference: **M7a**.
**Severity:** Medium (availability). **Confidence:** high in the cited source flow. No runtime reproduction, exploit input, destructive testing, or source changes; resource-exhaustion consequences have not been measured.

## Root cause and evidence
The per-word [crates/proof/src/lib.rs:490–496](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/proof/src/lib.rs#L490-L496) searches backward/forward for whitespace and rescans the enclosing token for internet markers. Punctuation splits that same token into many words, each redoing the scan.

## Conditions and realistic impact
A long whitespace-free paragraph containing many punctuation-separated short words produces quadratic scanning. Public proof APIs are affected; the layout 100,000-byte cutoff bounds input size but does not remove quadratic work below it.

## Recommended remediation
Tokenize whitespace spans and compute internet classification once, then associate constituent word ranges with those token results.

## Suggested regression tests
Operation-count or scaling regression through public single/multilingual proof APIs for punctuation-separated words, with ignore_internet both enabled and disabled; include normal prose as a control.

title: Markdown delimiter searches escape the bracket lookahead work budget
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Scope and verification
Read-only source audit of upstream main at 159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0. Audit reference: **M7b**.
**Severity:** Medium (availability). **Confidence:** high in the cited source flow. No runtime reproduction, exploit input, destructive testing, or source changes; resource-exhaustion consequences have not been measured.

## Root cause and evidence
[crates/formats/src/markdown.rs:547–594](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/formats/src/markdown.rs#L547-L594) invokes find_backticks from bracket scanning without charging the nested suffix scan to the budget. Ordinary code-span parsing at [crates/formats/src/markdown.rs:724–740](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/formats/src/markdown.rs#L724-L740) also calls that unbudgeted search. The budget update at [crates/formats/src/markdown.rs:769–775](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/formats/src/markdown.rs#L769-L775) accounts for outer distance, not nested work.

## Conditions and realistic impact
Multiple unmatched delimiter-run lengths cause repeated suffix scans and superlinear CPU work. The prior plain-unmatched-bracket case is fixed; this report is the residual nested/code-delimiter path. Exact timing/complexity thresholds were not measured.

## Recommended remediation
Share work accounting across all lookahead, or pre-index delimiter runs by position/length. Make budget exhaustion deterministic without repeatedly rescanning suffixes.

## Suggested regression tests
Public Markdown import combining unmatched brackets and different nonmatching backtick runs under an instrumented/small work budget; include matched spans and ordinary unmatched brackets as controls.

title: JSON document import accepts invalid run lengths and UTF-8 boundaries
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Scope and verification
Read-only audit of upstream main at 159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0. Audit reference: **M8**.
**Severity:** medium. **Confidence:** high in the cited source behavior. Static review only: no runtime reproduction, exploit input, destructive test, or source change.

## Root cause and evidence
[crates/engine/src/io.rs:119–125](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/engine/src/io.rs#L119-L125) deserializes Document and only calls ensure_nonempty. [crates/doc/src/para.rs:942–949](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/doc/src/para.rs#L942-L949) sums supplied run lengths unchecked; [crates/doc/src/para.rs:1027–1051](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/doc/src/para.rs#L1027-L1051) also merges/sums before repairing total coverage, without ensuring character-boundary run ends. Checked string consumers skip invalid slices in layout and DOCX output.

## Conditions and realistic impact
Imported runs ending inside a multibyte character can silently omit text from output. Oversized run lengths can panic in overflow-checked builds or wrap in release. This is not a claim that the checked string consumers themselves perform unsafe slicing.

## Recommended remediation
Validate/canonicalize model invariants at JSON ingress: checked lengths and sums, exact coverage, character boundaries, object correspondence, references and supported nesting. Return explicit errors rather than silently losing text.

## Suggested regression tests
Public JSON open followed by layout/export using split multibyte runs, excessive lengths, missing coverage and surplus object markers. Assert correct preservation or an import error, with no panic.

title: Document part and numbering ID allocation can overflow and collide with existing IDs
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Scope and verification
Read-only audit of upstream main at 159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0. Audit reference: **M9**.
**Severity:** medium. **Confidence:** high in the cited source behavior. Static review only: no runtime reproduction, exploit input, destructive test, or source change.

## Root cause and evidence
[crates/doc/src/lib.rs:885–892](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/doc/src/lib.rs#L885-L892) calculates max part key + 1 and inserts without collision/exhaustion checking. [crates/doc/src/numbering.rs:219–230](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/doc/src/numbering.rs#L219-L230) uses unchecked +1 for abstract/instance IDs. JSON models can supply maximum IDs.

## Conditions and realistic impact
Adding a part/list to an imported maximum-ID document can panic in checked builds or wrap in release. Wrapped part ID 0 can overwrite an existing story; numbering collisions can select unintended definitions. Session panic rollback does not prevent release-mode collisions or protect direct model callers.

## Recommended remediation
Use checked, collision-free allocation returning an explicit exhaustion error. Preserve existing resources on all failures.

## Suggested regression tests
Maximum-ID inputs with occupied low IDs. Assert either valid unused allocation or error and exact preservation of existing parts/lists; cover direct API and command calls.

title: Text-box pruning loses references below the model walker depth despite DOCX accepting deeper tables
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Scope and verification
Read-only audit of upstream main at 159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0. Audit reference: **M10**.
**Severity:** medium. **Confidence:** high in the cited source behavior. Static review only: no runtime reproduction, exploit input, destructive test, or source change.

## Root cause and evidence
[crates/docx/src/read/story.rs:202–206](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/docx/src/read/story.rs#L202-L206) accepts table nesting up to its MAX_TABLE_DEPTH=24. [crates/doc/src/lib.rs:1274–1287](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/doc/src/lib.rs#L1274-L1287) stops paragraph traversal above depth 16. [crates/doc/src/lib.rs:925–934](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/doc/src/lib.rs#L925-L934) prunes text-box parts using reachability from that incomplete traversal; successful mutating commands call pruning at [crates/engine/src/session.rs:1212–1220](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/engine/src/session.rs#L1212-L1220).

## Conditions and realistic impact
A text box referenced only from an accepted table deeper than 16 is treated as unreachable. An unrelated successful edit can delete its story. The mismatch also omits deeper content from other model traversal operations.

## Recommended remediation
Use complete iterative traversal or enforce one consistent model acceptance/traversal limit. Never equate traversal-budget exhaustion with unreachability.

## Suggested regression tests
Import a depth-17 table containing a text-box reference, perform an unrelated edit, and round-trip it. Assert the part, reference and text survive; add a genuinely unreferenced box control.

title: Layout style indices silently alias after 65,536 distinct paragraph styles
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Scope and verification
Read-only audit of upstream main at 159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0. Audit reference: **M11**.
**Severity:** medium. **Confidence:** high in the cited source behavior. Static review only: no runtime reproduction, exploit input, destructive test, or source change.

## Root cause and evidence
[crates/layout/src/para.rs:687–690](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/layout/src/para.rs#L687-L690) clamps self.styles.len() to u16::MAX but still appends each new style and returns the clamped index. Later runs consequently address an earlier StyleRun.

## Conditions and realistic impact
A paragraph with more than 65,536 distinct resolved formats can render later runs with the wrong metrics, link or revision visibility. Ordinary unequal formats suffice; NaN input is not required. Full-format equality now fixes the older incomplete-dedup-key defect, but not index exhaustion.

## Recommended remediation
Widen the index representation or return an explicit limit before appending beyond it. Do not silently substitute another style.

## Suggested regression tests
Distinct resolved styles spanning the boundary with different links and deletion flags as well as appearance. Verify observable layout/display behavior or explicit rejection.

title: Processing limits silently truncate layout, mail merge, LaTeX input and deep DOCX output
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Scope and verification
Read-only audit of upstream main at 159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0. Audit reference: **M12**.
**Severity:** medium. **Confidence:** high in the cited source behavior. Static review only: no runtime reproduction, exploit input, destructive test, or source change.

## Root cause and evidence
Four successful-but-incomplete limit paths:
- [crates/layout/src/para.rs:2061–2063](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/layout/src/para.rs#L2061-L2063) breaks paragraph layout at its line cap.
- [crates/engine/src/cmd/mailings.rs:634–665](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/engine/src/cmd/mailings.rs#L634-L665) stops merge output at the block cap and returns success.
- [crates/formats/src/latex.rs:1013–1017](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/formats/src/latex.rs#L1013-L1017) imports only the first 32 MiB.
- [crates/docx/src/write/story.rs:16–33](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/docx/src/write/story.rs#L16-L33) substitutes an empty paragraph beyond combined block depth.

## Conditions and realistic impact
Inputs/output exceeding these limits lose suffix text, recipients, or nested content while callers cannot distinguish complete output from truncation. Mail merge now accurately reports emitted record count; the remaining defect is omitted-record disclosure, not that old counting error.

## Recommended remediation
Return explicit limit errors before committing output, or a structured partial-result diagnostic requiring acknowledgement. Separate table/textbox budgets where appropriate; retain limits without silently dropping data.

## Suggested regression tests
Boundary and boundary-plus-one cases with recognizable suffix content. Assert full output or explicit error/partial status. For merge distinguish requested, emitted…

title: ODT/table and spreadsheet import silently omit repetitions or treat malformed XML as EOF
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Scope and verification
Read-only audit of upstream main at 159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0. Audit reference: **M13**.
**Severity:** medium. **Confidence:** high in the cited source behavior. Static review only: no runtime reproduction, exploit input, destructive test, or source change.

## Root cause and evidence
[crates/formats/src/odt.rs:1163–1177](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/formats/src/odt.rs#L1163-L1177) and [crates/formats/src/odt.rs:1239–1255](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/formats/src/odt.rs#L1239-L1255) append ODT table rows/cells once, ignoring repetition counts (ODS has a separate repetition implementation). Event helpers [crates/formats/src/odt.rs:687–718](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/formats/src/odt.rs#L687-L718) and [crates/formats/src/sheet.rs:226–268](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/formats/src/sheet.rs#L226-L268) end parsing on XML errors as if EOF, allowing partial successful results.

## Conditions and realistic impact
Valid repeated populated ODT rows/cells disappear, while repeated blanks shift later content. A valid XML prefix followed by corruption can import as a successful partial document/recipient list and be resaved or merged with missing content.

## Recommended remediation
Implement bounded ODT repeat expansion with span/covered-cell semantics. Propagate parse errors separately from EOF or expose explicit recovery/truncation status that callers cannot mistake for full success.

## Suggested regression tests
ODT repeated populated rows/cells/interior blanks and excessive counts; ODT/XLSX/ODS valid prefixes followed by malformed XML. Require complete preservation or explicit failure/recovery status.

title: DOCX embedded-object preservation reports success when descendant resources were dropped
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Scope and verification
Read-only audit of upstream main at 159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0. Audit reference: **M14-graph**.
**Severity:** medium. **Confidence:** high in the cited source behavior. Static review only: no runtime reproduction, exploit input, destructive test, or source change.

## Root cause and evidence
[crates/docx/src/read/embed.rs:75–107](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/docx/src/read/embed.rs#L75-L107) considers keep_part_tree successful once the root survives; unavailable/over-budget descendants and truncated relationships are skipped. [crates/docx/src/write/embed.rs:219–255](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/docx/src/write/embed.rs#L219-L255) can omit descendant relationships and still serialize the root. Root object-markup validation does not establish transitive graph completeness.

## Conditions and realistic impact
Charts/diagrams/OLE roots with missing or budget-rejected second-hop resources can be saved with incomplete dependencies. Logs do not expose loss through the successful public save result. Related #1034 covers general unmodelled markup/part preservation; this is completeness of the existing embedded graph preservation mechanism, following closed #319.

## Recommended remediation
Track graph completeness and return a preservation/loss diagnostic when any required descendant cannot be retained. Handle graph cycles without confusing visited nodes with missing resources.

## Suggested regression tests
Public DOCX read/write with an existing root and missing second-hop descendant, graph-budget exhaustion, and cycles. Require explicit degraded/error status or faithful retention, rather than unqualified preservation.

title: Document Inspector misses hidden text outside the body and hidden formatting inherited from styles
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Scope and verification
Read-only audit of upstream main at 159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0. Audit reference: **M15**.
**Severity:** medium. **Confidence:** high in the cited source behavior. Static review only: no runtime reproduction, exploit input, destructive test, or source change.

## Root cause and evidence
[crates/engine/src/cmd/tools.rs:1265–1301](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/engine/src/cmd/tools.rs#L1265-L1301) detects/removes only body runs with direct hidden == Some(true). It does not traverse other stories or resolve style-inherited hidden state. The result echoes requested removals at line 1311.

## Conditions and realistic impact
Hidden text in headers, footers, text boxes or styles survives an inspection/removal intended to prepare a document for disclosure. The success-shaped response can mislead users about residual sensitive content.

## Recommended remediation
Inspect all relevant stories using effective formatting, remove matching content consistently, and report unsupported/residual content explicitly rather than implying complete sanitization.

## Suggested regression tests
Direct and style-inherited hidden content in body and non-body stories. Run public inspection/removal, round-trip the result and verify no targeted sensitive text remains; include visible-text controls.

title: Deleting comments leaves non-body anchors and nested reply descendants dangling
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Scope and verification
Read-only audit of upstream main at 159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0. Audit reference: **M16**.
**Severity:** medium. **Confidence:** high in the cited source behavior. Static review only: no runtime reproduction, exploit input, destructive test, or source change.

## Root cause and evidence
[crates/engine/src/cmd/review.rs:187–226](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/engine/src/cmd/review.rs#L187-L226) traverses Body only when removing anchors and includes only direct replies when collecting definitions to delete. [crates/engine/src/cmd/review.rs:141–150](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/engine/src/cmd/review.rs#L141-L150) permits replies to existing replies.

## Conditions and realistic impact
Deleting a header/text-box comment leaves anchors referencing removed definitions. Deleting a root with a reply-to-reply leaves a descendant whose parent was removed. This is a source-model integrity issue distinct from UI controls in #1082.

## Recommended remediation
Traverse anchors in all stories and compute the complete reply descendant closure before removing definitions/parts. Preserve undo behavior.

## Suggested regression tests
Non-body anchors and a three-level reply chain through public commands; assert no dangling anchors/parents/parts after deletion, and complete restoration after Undo.

title: Paragraph dialog normalizes untouched mixed formatting and creates multiple undo steps
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Scope and verification
Read-only audit of upstream main at 159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0. Audit reference: **M17**.
**Severity:** medium. **Confidence:** high in the cited source behavior. Static review only: no runtime reproduction, exploit input, destructive test, or source change.

## Root cause and evidence
[crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs.rs:995–1021](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs.rs#L995-L1021) initializes from the caret paragraph, not mixed-selection state. [crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs.rs:2837–2860](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs.rs#L2837-L2860) unconditionally dispatches direction, alignment and a primary-property update, even when only one field changed.

## Conditions and realistic impact
Select differently formatted paragraphs, open Paragraph and accept or edit one setting. Untouched properties can be replaced by caret-paragraph values. Multiple mutating calls make one dialog action several undo steps. Fixed line spacing and some ancillary fields have improved change handling; those fixes do not cover the primary mixed fields.

## Recommended remediation
Track mixed values and changed-field masks for all fields; leave untouched properties unset and apply the dialog as one transaction.

## Suggested regression tests
Mixed paragraphs with unchanged OK and a one-field edit. Assert unchanged unrelated properties and exactly one undo step restoring the entire dialog action.

title: Comment drafts are keyed only by comment ID and removed before a failed commit can be recovered
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Scope and verification
Read-only audit of upstream main at 159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0. Audit reference: **M19**.
**Severity:** medium. **Confidence:** High for draft key/removal defects; medium for close/focus ordering consequences. No runtime reproduction, exploit input, destructive testing or source modification.

## Root cause and evidence
[crates/ui-egui/src/panes.rs:409–445](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/ui-egui/src/panes.rs#L409-L445) stores temporary drafts by comment ID, commits only on focus loss, removes the draft before review.editComment, and discards that command result. [crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs:704–712](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs#L704-L712) resets other state on document replacement but not these draft keys; close eligibility at [crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs:838–847](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs#L838-L847) uses session dirty state.

## Conditions and realistic impact
A refused protected edit loses its draft. A replacement document reusing a comment ID can consume stale draft text. Focused draft-only edits may bypass a close prompt if lifecycle processing precedes focus-loss commit; that specific GUI timing remains unverified. The old direct-mutation/no-undo issue is fixed and is not alleged here.

## Recommended remediation
Scope drafts by document identity; flush/validate them before save/replacement/close, retain them on command failure, and clear only after successful persistence or explicit discard.

## Suggested regression tests
Failed commit retains typed text; replacement documents with the same comment ID never inherit drafts; focused comment edits participate in save/close decisions. Exercise real focus/lifecycle ordering.

title: Web image paste listener inserts into the document without checking the active edit target
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Scope and verification
Read-only audit of upstream main at 159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0. Audit reference: **M20**.
**Severity:** medium. **Confidence:** High in cited source flow; runtime consequences not reproduced. No runtime reproduction, exploit input, destructive testing or source modification.

## Root cause and evidence
[apps/wordcraft-web/src/web.rs:161–195](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/apps/wordcraft-web/src/web.rs#L161-L195) registers a document-wide image-paste listener that checks clipboard content but not canvas ownership/focus. Queued images become document insertions at [crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs:1569–1570](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs#L1569-L1570).

## Conditions and realistic impact
Pasting an image-only clipboard while focus is in a comment, Find field or dialog can insert a picture at the retained document selection instead of respecting the active editor.

## Recommended remediation
Route paste using explicit edit-target ownership. Only enqueue canvas image insertion when the document canvas is the intended target; retain appropriate default behavior in other fields.

## Suggested regression tests
Image-only paste with canvas, comment, Find and dialog focus. Assert document changes only for the canvas case and no duplicate insertion from multiple event handlers.

title: Document::delete_range can partially mutate the document before returning an error
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Scope and verification
Read-only audit of upstream main at 159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0. Audit reference: **M21**.
**Severity:** medium. **Confidence:** High in cited source flow; runtime consequences not reproduced. No runtime reproduction, exploit input, destructive testing or source modification.

## Root cause and evidence
[crates/doc/src/edit.rs:317–366](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/doc/src/edit.rs#L317-L366) trims the first endpoint before resolving/validating the second and subsequent fallible operations. The different-container branch likewise edits before establishing all endpoint validity.

## Conditions and realistic impact
A valid first endpoint and invalid second path/UTF-8 offset can leave text removed despite Err. Session::run rollback protects ordinary mutating commands when errors propagate, but direct model callers do not get atomicity; integration paths therefore need particular care.

## Recommended remediation
Validate all endpoints and fallible prerequisites before mutation, or stage the operation transactionally. Document the public API guarantee and do not rely on every caller to reconstruct rollback.

## Suggested regression tests
Direct public delete_range with an invalid second endpoint and cross-container failure; assert exact document equality on Err. Include valid deletion and engine rollback controls.

title: Restart Numbering discards the source list instance level overrides
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Scope and verification
Read-only audit of upstream main at 159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0. Audit reference: **M22**.
**Severity:** medium. **Confidence:** High in cited source flow; runtime consequences not reproduced. No runtime reproduction, exploit input, destructive testing or source modification.

## Root cause and evidence
[crates/doc/src/numbering.rs:226–230](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/doc/src/numbering.rs#L226-L230) creates a new Num from the abstract ID/start values plus defaults, without copying level_overrides or preserving the source effective level definitions.

## Conditions and realistic impact
Restarting an imported list with instance-specific number format, label text or indentation can change those properties as well as its starting value. This is independent of ID-allocation overflow tracked in #1338.

## Recommended remediation
Copy effective level overrides into the new instance and explicitly define which start overrides Restart resets. Preserve unrelated numbering appearance.

## Suggested regression tests
Restart an imported list with overridden format, label and indentation, plus overridden starts. Assert only intended start values change and round-trip preserves the custom appearance.

title: PAGE fields after intra-paragraph page breaks or continuation can show the initial page number
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Scope and verification
Read-only audit of upstream main at 159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0. Audit reference: **M23**.
**Severity:** medium. **Confidence:** Medium–high; source-flow conclusion, not rendered reproduction. No runtime reproduction, exploit input, destructive testing or source modification.

## Root cause and evidence
[crates/layout/src/lib.rs:2523–2524](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/layout/src/lib.rs#L2523-L2524) sets field page context before shaping. [crates/layout/src/lib.rs:2771–2775](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/layout/src/lib.rs#L2771-L2775) reuses that paragraph layout for fragments; [crates/layout/src/lib.rs:2957–2984](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/layout/src/lib.rs#L2957-L2984) advances pages without generally reshaping remaining PAGE fields (column-width relayout is a separate special case).

## Conditions and realistic impact
A PAGE field after an explicit page break within one paragraph, or on a natural continuation page, can retain the value from initial shaping. Body NUMPAGES/SECTIONPAGES totals have a separate fix and are not included in this report.

## Recommended remediation
Resolve page-sensitive fields per placed fragment and account for width changes when relaying out remaining content.

## Suggested regression tests
PAGE after an intra-paragraph page break and on natural continuation, including crossing a page-number digit-width boundary. Compare actual field/display output against final placement.

title: Flat OPC outer parsing lacks depth/work accounting and ignores CDATA binary content
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Scope and verification
Read-only audit of upstream main at 159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0. Audit reference: **M24**.
**Severity:** medium. **Confidence:** High for missing guards/event handling; medium for practical resource-exhaustion consequences. No runtime reproduction, exploit input, destructive testing or source modification.

## Root cause and evidence
[crates/docx/src/flat.rs:100–198](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/docx/src/flat.rs#L100-L198) increments outer depth without a maximum and materializes XML/binary text before downstream checks. [crates/docx/src/flat.rs:237–247](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/docx/src/flat.rs#L237-L247) accounts accepted unique stored parts, not all duplicate/unused processing. Binary handling accepts Text events but leaves CDATA/general-reference representations unhandled.

## Conditions and realistic impact
Deep/large unused or duplicate outer structures consume work outside ordinary DOCX tree limits. Valid CDATA representations can produce missing binary part bytes. The public source-size cap remains a mitigation; unlimited source input is not claimed.

## Recommended remediation
Enforce outer event/depth and prospective allocation budgets, count processed work independently of stored unique parts, and support or explicitly reject valid alternative binary-text event forms.

## Suggested regression tests
Public read_xml with small depth/work budgets, deep/duplicate parts, and equivalent Text versus CDATA binary encodings; require faithful content or explicit error.

title: Font family caches retain arbitrary keys and math resolution ignores font-generation changes
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Scope and verification
Read-only audit of upstream main at 159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0. Audit reference: **M25**.
**Severity:** medium. **Confidence:** High in cited source flow; runtime consequences not reproduced. No runtime reproduction, exploit input, destructive testing or source modification.

## Root cause and evidence
[crates/fonts/src/word.rs:195–225](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/fonts/src/word.rs#L195-L225) retains general family keys without an entry/byte cap. [crates/fonts/src/math.rs:304–325](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/fonts/src/math.rs#L304-L325) maintains a permanent math-family cache without generation checks; user font changes bump generation at [crates/fonts/src/fontdb/user.rs:306–339](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/fonts/src/fontdb/user.rs#L306-L339).

## Conditions and realistic impact
Many distinct requested families across documents accumulate memory. Resolving math before adding/removing an appropriate font can keep stale resolution after relayout. Existing outline/fallback cache limits are not implicated; this is not the already-fixed per-character font reread problem.

## Recommended remediation
Bound retained key bytes/entries, generation-invalidate math resolution and evict obsolete face metadata where appropriate.

## Suggested regression tests
Many missing family names with observable bounded cache policy; resolve–install–resolve and resolve–remove–resolve math fonts. Assert chosen results reflect database changes.

title: Print-to-PDF and PNG export still overwrite destinations directly instead of using safe replacement
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Scope and verification
Read-only audit of upstream main at 159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0. Audit reference: **M26**.
**Severity:** medium. **Confidence:** High in cited source flow; runtime consequences not reproduced. No runtime reproduction, exploit input, destructive testing or source modification.

## Root cause and evidence
[crates/engine/src/io.rs:408–410](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/engine/src/io.rs#L408-L410) writes with fs::write, which truncates an existing destination before writing. Print-to-PDF calls it at [crates/engine/src/print.rs:160–166](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/engine/src/print.rs#L160-L166) and PNG export at [crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs:227–238](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/engine/src/cmd/file.rs#L227-L238). Normal document saves already have an owned temporary-file replacement path.

## Conditions and realistic impact
Overwriting an existing output followed by a short write, disk-full error or interruption can leave the previous output destroyed/incomplete. This is not a claim that the redesigned normal document safe-save remains broken.

## Recommended remediation
Reuse safe-save preparation/replacement for these output files, with the same owned-temp cleanup and permissions handling.

## Suggested regression tests
Inject preparation/write failures with disposable output files and assert the existing destination stays intact and only owned temporary files are removed.

title: MCP type_text overwrites a failed newParagraph result with a later insertion success
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Scope and verification
Read-only audit of upstream main at 159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0. Audit reference: **M27-type**.
**Severity:** medium. **Confidence:** High in cited source flow; runtime consequences not reproduced. No runtime reproduction, exploit input, destructive testing or source modification.

## Root cause and evidence
[crates/mcp/src/tools.rs:233–240](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/mcp/src/tools.rs#L233-L240) stores the result of text.newParagraph, then overwrites it with text.insert for a nonempty next line without first checking the paragraph result.

## Conditions and realistic impact
When a paragraph break is refused but insertion is otherwise possible, multiline typing may concatenate content and report success despite the failed break. Even if insertion also fails, the original failure is hidden.

## Recommended remediation
Check and propagate each command result before issuing the next operation; consider transactional semantics for the complete multiline operation.

## Suggested regression tests
Controlled backend where newParagraph fails and insertion would succeed: require the original error and no subsequent insertion. Include successful multiline typing and empty-line cases.

title: Corpus downloader fetches an unauthenticated HTTP archive and extracts it without a pinned digest
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Scope and verification
Read-only audit of upstream main at 159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0. Audit reference: **M28**.
**Severity:** medium. **Confidence:** High in cited source flow; runtime consequences not reproduced. No runtime reproduction, exploit input, destructive testing or source modification.

## Root cause and evidence
[xtask/src/main.rs:202–231](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/xtask/src/main.rs#L202-L231) downloads PngSuite via plain HTTP, has no content digest verification and immediately invokes tar extraction.

## Conditions and realistic impact
Running cargo xtask corpus --download on a compromised network can substitute test inputs and submit untrusted archive contents to tar. Exact archive-escape behavior is platform-dependent and was not tested; no compromise is alleged.

## Recommended remediation
Use HTTPS plus a pinned digest, verify before extraction, and constrain archive member paths/types and extraction location.

## Suggested regression tests
Digest mismatch prevents extraction; reject unsafe absolute/parent-traversal/link members in a disposable test harness; accept the pinned expected archive.

title: Release hardening: review the explicit trust in a mutable privileged shared-workflow branch
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Scope and verification
Read-only source audit of upstream main at 159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0. Audit reference: **H11**.
**Severity:** High conditional supply-chain risk; intentional policy, not demonstrated compromise. **Confidence:** high for the cited source/configuration. Static review only; no runtime reproduction, destructive test, or source change. No compromise is alleged.

## Root cause and evidence
[.github/workflows/release.yml:13–43](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/.github/workflows/release.yml#L13-L43) grants contents:write and explicitly passes signing credentials to storytold/craft-common-actions/.github/workflows/release.yml@main. The preceding comment expressly states this is intentional so shared changes propagate without PR churn. The font input is already pinned.

## Conditions and realistic impact
A compromised or erroneous change to that external branch changes release execution without a corresponding reviewable change here. This issue records the tradeoff for maintainers; it does not claim the configuration is accidental or that the external repository is compromised.

## Recommended remediation
Consider pinning the workflow to reviewed commits with automated update PRs, and minimizing credentials/permissions. If mutable trust remains an accepted policy, document the branch-protection/review controls that justify it.

## Suggested regression checks
A policy check can reject mutable privileged references unless explicitly allowlisted with rationale; inspect credential/permission scope during workflow updates. No release workflow was triggered by this audit.

title: Measurement parser checks finiteness before unit conversion but can return infinity
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Scope and verification
Read-only source audit of upstream main at 159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0. Audit reference: **L1**.
**Severity:** Low. **Confidence:** high for the cited source/configuration. Static review only; no runtime reproduction, destructive test, or source change. No compromise is alleged.

## Root cause and evidence
[crates/geom/src/lib.rs:112–127](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/geom/src/lib.rs#L112-L127) validates the parsed f32, then returns Some(v * k) without checking the multiplication result.

## Conditions and realistic impact
A finite near-maximum decimal value in inches/centimeters/picas/lines can overflow during conversion and be accepted as an infinite measurement. Downstream GUI effects were not established.

## Recommended remediation
Check the converted result for finiteness and reject overflow with None/the established parse error.

## Suggested regression checks
Large finite inputs for each scaled unit, positive/negative boundaries, and ordinary measurements; assert accepted results are always finite.

title: RTF Unicode font names bypass the u/uc decoder in FontTbl
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Scope and verification
Read-only source audit of upstream main at 159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0. Audit reference: **L2**.
**Severity:** Low (format fidelity). **Confidence:** high for the cited source/configuration. Static review only; no runtime reproduction, destructive test, or source change. No compromise is alleged.

## Root cause and evidence
[crates/formats/src/rtf.rs:1220–1232](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/formats/src/rtf.rs#L1220-L1232) handles font/code-page controls and returns unconditionally for FontTbl, so Unicode u/uc controls never reach the normal decoding/fallback-skip path. Metadata/bookmark/field-instruction Unicode was fixed separately.

## Conditions and realistic impact
Unicode-escaped non-ASCII font names can retain fallback text or lose characters, leading to incorrect substitution and corrupted names in later conversion. This is narrower than closed #435 and does not reopen its fixed destinations.

## Recommended remediation
Allow u/uc handling through the font-table destination while retaining font-specific control handling and routing decoded characters to the font-name accumulator.

## Suggested regression checks
Public RTF import/export/import of Unicode font names with ordinary fallback, hex fallback, and uc0, plus body runs using those fonts.

title: Desktop preferences overwrite ui.json non-atomically and discard write failures
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Scope and verification
Read-only source audit of upstream main at 159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0. Audit reference: **L3**.
**Severity:** Low (settings reliability). **Confidence:** high for the cited source/configuration. Static review only; no runtime reproduction, destructive test, or source change. No compromise is alleged.

## Root cause and evidence
[apps/wordcraft/src/main.rs:187–197](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/apps/wordcraft/src/main.rs#L187-L197) serializes preferences and directly calls fs::write, ignoring directory/write failures.

## Conditions and realistic impact
Interrupted or failed writes can truncate/lose preferences without feedback. Concurrent instances can overwrite each other settings; no document-content corruption is alleged in this preferences path.

## Recommended remediation
Prepare an owned sibling temporary file and replace only after success, surface persistence errors, and define multi-instance ownership/merge behavior.

## Suggested regression checks
Injected preparation/replacement failure preserves the old preferences and reports an error; concurrent-instance behavior follows the chosen policy.

title: Web font persistence waits for IndexedDB request success, not transaction completion
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Scope and verification
Read-only source audit of upstream main at 159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0. Audit reference: **L4**.
**Severity:** Low (persistence reliability). **Confidence:** high for the cited source/configuration. Static review only; no runtime reproduction, destructive test, or source change. No compromise is alleged.

## Root cause and evidence
[apps/wordcraft-web/src/web/font_store.rs:53–64](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/apps/wordcraft-web/src/web/font_store.rs#L53-L64) returns once the put/delete request succeeds and does not await the containing transaction complete/abort/error events. Callers log only errors returned by these futures.

## Conditions and realistic impact
A transaction can abort after its individual request succeeded; the operation then appears successful internally and loses persistence without the promised failure log. Specific browser timing was not reproduced.

## Recommended remediation
Retain and await the transaction completion/abort result, propagate failures, and bound/serialize persistence as needed for lifecycle consistency.

## Suggested regression checks
Request success followed by transaction abort must report failure; completed transactions persist; rapid store/remove ordering should match the documented last operation.

title: Nested mutating command aliases create redundant undo checkpoints
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Scope and verification
Read-only source audit of upstream main at 159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0. Audit reference: **L5**.
**Severity:** Low (undo behavior). **Confidence:** high for the cited source/configuration. Static review only; no runtime reproduction, destructive test, or source change. No compromise is alleged.

## Root cause and evidence
[crates/engine/src/cmd/outline.rs:55–71](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/engine/src/cmd/outline.rs#L55-L71) registers mutating wrappers that invoke other mutating commands via s.run. [crates/engine/src/session.rs:1175–1179](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/crates/engine/src/session.rs#L1175-L1179) checkpoints each invocation without grouping those aliases.

## Conditions and realistic impact
One promote/demote/move operation can add two undo checkpoints, leading to redundant/no-op Undo steps. Existing nested-command error rollback tests do not establish correct successful grouping.

## Recommended remediation
Use shared internal implementations or explicit transaction/undo grouping for aliases so one user action contributes one checkpoint.

## Suggested regression checks
Invoke representative aliases through public Session::run; assert undo depth increases by exactly one and one Undo restores the prior document/selection.

title: Asset attribution gate can report success when git ls-files fails
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Scope and verification
Read-only source audit of upstream main at 159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0. Audit reference: **L6-assets**.
**Severity:** Low–medium (validation gate). **Confidence:** high for the cited source/configuration. Static review only; no runtime reproduction, destructive test, or source change. No compromise is alleged.

## Root cause and evidence
[xtask/src/assets.rs:27–37](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/xtask/src/assets.rs#L27-L37) checks whether git was spawned but never tests out.status. Empty stdout after a nonzero exit is treated as an empty file list and can print success.

## Conditions and realistic impact
Running outside a usable Git checkout or encountering a Git failure can bypass attribution validation. Line-based parsing also is not a robust representation of arbitrary Git paths. The failure path was source-reviewed, not executed.

## Recommended remediation
Reject nonzero subprocess status with a diagnostic and use NUL-delimited Git output for paths. Do not equate inability to enumerate files with a successful empty audit.

## Suggested regression checks
Controlled git subprocess failure must fail the gate; an unattributed tracked asset must fail; include path quoting/newline handling using a disposable test repository.

title: Dependency maintenance: PDF path retains unmaintained rustybuzz and ttf-parser
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Scope and verification
Read-only source audit of upstream main at 159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0. Audit reference: **Dependencies-maintenance**.
**Severity:** Low (maintenance risk; not a vulnerability claim). **Confidence:** high for the cited source/configuration. Static review only; no runtime reproduction, destructive test, or source change. No compromise is alleged.

## Root cause and evidence
[Cargo.lock:3477–3478](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/Cargo.lock#L3477-L3478) locks rustybuzz 0.20.1 and [Cargo.lock:4082–4083](https://github.com/storytold/wordcraft/blob/159b84f54c74e9e82fb3109b758ae7dd6f4e3ab0/Cargo.lock#L4082-L4083) locks ttf-parser 0.25.1. They are reached through the krilla PDF dependency path. Official advisories: https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0206.html and https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0192.html identify them as unmaintained, not vulnerable versions with a known exploit.

## Conditions and realistic impact
Future font correctness/security fixes may not reach this dependency path. The audit did not establish a memory-safety defect or exploitable vulnerability in either package. quick-xml is already 0.41.0, so its older cited advisories are not current findings.

## Recommended remediation
Track maintained krilla/dependency releases or migration to maintained alternatives (harfrust/skrifa as appropriate) and add automated advisory review with explicit treatment of maintenance notices.

## Suggested regression checks
Run the official advisory tool in CI after updating and validate PDF/font fixtures. The current audit used read-only lockfile/advisory version-range comparison, not cargo audit or target/feature reachability analysis.

title: Source audit follow-up: upstream main 159b84f — findings and verification limits
author: PierrunoYT

title: Layout: a paragraph continued into the next column doesn't wrap around a shape there
author: dkhlapov
body:
Found while working on #884 / PR #1139. A paragraph is broken into lines once, in the column where it starts (`anchor_floats` takes exclusions relative to that column). The lines that continue into the next column are reused as they are, so they run through a shape anchored or placed in that column.

Expected (Word): the continued lines wrap around the shape like any other text in that column.

Fix idea: after the paragraph moves to the next column, break its remaining lines again against that column's exclusions, without re-placing the paragraph's own floats. Related: #1158.

title: Linux: the interface always uses the embedded Inter; add an option to use the system interface font
author: musaad-sharikh
body:
WordCraft draws its ribbon, menus and dialogs in the embedded Inter, whatever the desktop's default interface font is, and File › Options has no setting to change it. On a desktop where every other application follows the fontconfig default, WordCraft is the one that does not.

### Use case

My fontconfig defaults are Rubik for `sans-serif` and Vazirmatn for Arabic. GTK and Qt applications follow them. I would like WordCraft's interface to do the same, or to let me pick the interface font. This is about the interface only, not document fonts.

### Current limitation

- Options offers "Interface size" (#475) but no interface font.
- The Flatpak sandbox already sees the user's fonts: `fc-match sans-serif` run inside it returns Rubik, and `fc-match sans-serif:lang=ar` returns Vazirmatn. The interface does not use either.

### Desired outcome

Either of:

- an "Interface font" setting in Options (system default, or a chosen installed family), with Inter kept as the default; or
- on Linux, resolve the interface font through fontconfig, so the user's defaults apply.

### Environment

- WordCraft 0.6.1, Flatpak (`org.freedesktop.Platform` 25.08), x86_64
- CachyOS Linux, niri 26.04, Wayland

### Where it comes from (v0.6.1)

`font_definitions()` in `crates/ui-egui/src/theme.rs` embeds Inter (Regular, Medium, SemiBold) and JetBrains Mono and inserts Inter first in the proportional family.

Related: storytold/gridcraft#229, storytold/photocraft#2291.

title: DOCX → PDF: text flows to the right of a square-wrapped floating picture and is clipped at the page edge
author: mmazzieri
body:
_Written by an AI assistant (Claude) at the request of @mmazzieri._

**Version:** wordcraft-cli 0.6.1 (Windows x64); still on main 159b84f.

**Steps:** `wordcraft-cli convert S03-immagini.docx out.pdf` (synthetic file; it follows in a comment, with a side-by-side image: left Aspose.Words 20.10, right WordCraft).

**Expected:** on page 1, a 150×150 pt picture anchored to the paragraph (`wp:anchor`, `wp:wrapSquare wrapText="bothSides"`), placed 300 pt from the margin, so it sits at the right of the single text column. The paragraph wraps on its left only, because there's no usable room on its right. This is how Word and Aspose.Words lay it out.

**Actual:** the lines go on to the right of the picture, up to and past the right margin. Words are cut at the page edge ("docu", "operat", "registr").

**Notes:** this is a single-column page, so it's a different case from #884 (a dragged shape) and #1158 (multi-column). Word leaves out a strip beside a wrapped object when it's narrower than a minimum width. Here the strip to the right of the picture is too narrow, yet WordCraft still puts text in it and clips it.

title: DOCX: VML preset shapes (e.g. right arrow, _x0000_t13) are not drawn
author: mmazzieri
body:
_Written by an AI assistant (Claude) at the request of @mmazzieri._

**Version:** wordcraft-cli 0.6.1 (Windows x64); still on main 159b84f.

**Steps:** `wordcraft-cli convert S03-immagini.docx out.pdf` (the same synthetic file as the wrap issue; it follows in a comment).

**Expected:** an inline orange right arrow before the caption "flusso del paziente dal triage al reparto". In the file it's a VML shape, `<w:pict><v:shapetype id="_x0000_t13" o:spt="13" …><v:shape type="#_x0000_t13" fillcolor="…">`, the preset right arrow (shape type 13).

**Actual:** nothing is drawn; only the caption shows.

**Where:** `crates/docx/src/read/story.rs` `read_vml` handles pictures, text boxes, `v:line`, `v:rect`, `v:roundrect` and `v:oval`, and returns `None` for any other `v:shape` (`_ => return None`). So VML preset shapes referenced through `type="#_x0000_tNN"` (arrows, stars, callouts…) are dropped. Mapping the common `o:spt` values to the DrawingML presets WordCraft already draws would cover most of them.

title: Linux/Hyprland: WordCraft defaults to XWayland and renders ~2x oversized at fractional scale (GridCraft runs native Wayland and is fine)
author: BluePhi09
body:
## Summary

On Hyprland with fractional scaling, WordCraft 0.6.1 runs via XWayland by default and renders at roughly 2× the intended size. GridCraft 0.6.1 on the same machine runs natively on Wayland and scales correctly (see screenshot comparison: GridCraft top, WordCraft bottom, both at 100% zoom).

## Environment

- Arch Linux, Hyprland (Wayland session, `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` and `DISPLAY` both set)
- Laptop panel eDP-1: 2880x1800 @ 120 Hz, Hyprland scale **1.25**
- `xwayland:force_zero_scaling = false`, no `Xft.dpi` in `xrdb`, no XSETTINGS daemon
- WordCraft 0.6.1 (7dfa6b0e) AppImage, GridCraft 0.6.1 AppImage (both winit 0.30.13)

## Observed

```
$ hyprctl clients
class: ai.storyteller.wordcraft   xwayland: 1
class: ai.storyteller.gridcraft   xwayland: 0
```

WordCraft log:
```
WARN [main] winit::platform_impl::linux::x11::xdisplay: error setting XSETTINGS; Xft options won't reload automatically
```

Without `Xft.dpi`, winit's X11 backend falls back to computing the scale factor from RandR physical size, which on this HiDPI panel gives a much larger factor than the compositor's 1.25, so the whole UI (ribbon, ruler, status bar) is oversized.

## Workarounds that work

- `env -u DISPLAY wordcraft` → runs natively on Wayland (`xwayland: 0`) and scales correctly, same as GridCraft
- (presumably) `WORDCRAFT_WAYLAND=1`, as mentioned in #1240
- `WINIT_X11_SCALE_FACTOR=1.25` should pin the X11 factor

`WINIT_UNIX_BACKEND=wayland` has no effect.

## Expected

Either:
1. Use native Wayland when `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` is set (as GridCraft does), or at least on compositors where the XWayland-default reasons (clipboard/IME, cf. #1213, #1169) don't apply, or
2. When staying on X11, avoid the RandR DPI fallback when no `Xft.dpi` is available (e.g. default to 1.0 and let the compositor scale, or respect the Interface size setting from #1142).

Related: #822, #1240.

title: Right-click created Word documents (.docx) are not recognized properly and trigger "Save As" on edit
author: francescodauria
body:
#### Summary
When creating a new Word document directly through the Windows context menu (`Right-click -> New -> Microsoft Word Document`), opening this file with WorldCraft fails to recognize it as an existing document session. When attempting to save edits, WorldCraft does not save back to the file; instead, it triggers a "Save As" dialog prompting to create another file.

#### Steps to Reproduce
1. In Windows File Explorer (or Desktop), right-click in an empty space.
2. Select **New > Microsoft Word Document** (`.docx`).
3. Double-click or choose **Open with > WorldCraft** to open the newly created file.
4. Add any text or modifications.
5. Press `Ctrl + S` or click the **Save** button.

#### Expected Behavior
WorldCraft should:
- Correctly identify the file path of the opened `.docx`.
- Save modifications directly back into the existing file without opening a "Save As" prompt.

#### Current Behavior
WorldCraft treats the file as unsaved or detached from its file path. Saving prompts a "Save As" file picker dialog, forcing the user to select or overwrite a target file manually.

#### Possible Cause
Files generated via the Windows context menu (`ShellNew`) often start as empty 0-byte placeholders until populated and saved by an application. WorldCraft may fail to parse 0-byte `.docx` files or might lose the initial file handle/path binding upon initialization.

#### Environment
- **OS:** Windows 11
- **WorldCraft Version:** 0.6.1 (7dfa6b0e)

title: macOS: Native system menu bar (NSMenu) with standard File, Edit, View, Window menus
author: Osaym
body:
### Summary
On macOS, desktop productivity applications follow standard platform conventions by populating the system menu bar at the top of the screen (next to the Apple menu). For example, Microsoft Word for Mac provides top-level menus (`File`, `Edit`, `View`, `Insert`, `Format`, `Tools`, `Table`, `Window`, `Help`) that allow users to access core document workflows, discover keyboard shortcuts, and use macOS Accessibility/Menu navigation.

Currently, WordCraft on macOS only registers the basic application menu (` WordCraft`) created by the windowing runtime (`winit`), leaving the top system menu bar empty while all actions remain inside the in-window ribbon.

### Expected Behavior
On macOS, WordCraft should populate the native system menu bar (`NSMenu`) with standard application menus wired to WordCraft's existing command engine:
- **File**: New (`⌘N`), Open… (`⌘O`), Save (`⌘S`), Save As… (`⇧⌘S`), Close (`⌘W`), Print… (`⌘P`)
- **Edit**: Undo (`⌘Z`), Redo (`⌘Y` / `⇧⌘Z`), Cut (`⌘X`), Copy (`⌘C`), Paste (`⌘V`), Select All (`⌘A`)
- **View**: Print Layout, Reading Mode, Ruler, Navigation Pane, Zoom
- **Window**: Minimize (`⌘M`), Zoom, Bring All to Front
- **Help**: WordCraft Help

### Proposed Approach
Under `#[cfg(target_os = "macos")]`, construct an `NSMenu` hierarchy using `objc2-app-kit` and bind menu selections to WordCraft command IDs (`file.new`, `file.open`, `file.save`, `edit.undo`, etc.).

title: `wordcraft --control` takes the next argument as its port without checking it
author: Nael-Nathanael
body:
## Summary

`--control` reads whatever follows it as the port. When that isn't a valid port, or nothing follows, the app drops it and starts without the control channel, and says nothing.

## Repro (`upstream/main` `159b84f`)

`apps/wordcraft/src/main.rs:245`:

```rust
"--control" => control_port = args.next().and_then(|p| p.parse().ok()),
```

- `wordcraft --control --help` opens the app. `--help` is taken as the port, fails to parse and is dropped, so neither help nor the control channel starts. With #977 merged, `wordcraft --help` prints the usage, but this order still doesn't.
- `wordcraft --control --sample` opens a blank document: `--sample` is used up the same way.
- `wordcraft --control 79811` or `wordcraft --control abc` opens the app with no control channel and no message. The port is a `u16`, so 79811 doesn't parse.
- `wordcraft --control` as the last argument does the same.
- A bad `--control` also clears a port set in `WORDCRAFT_CONTROL_PORT` (line 239), since the parse result overwrites it.

## Expected

- `--control` followed by a flag (`--help`, `-h`, `--sample`) leaves the flag to be read as a flag.
- A missing or invalid port prints an error naming the bad value and exits non-zero, rather than starting without the channel.

## Related

#968, #977 (`--help` for the app and the CLI).

title: `wordcraft-cli` and `wordcraft` panic on a file name that isn't valid UTF-8
author: Nael-Nathanael
body:
## Summary

Both binaries read their arguments with `std::env::args()`, which panics when an argument isn't valid Unicode. A file name in a legacy encoding crashes them before they look at it.

## Repro (`upstream/main` `159b84f`, Linux)

```
$ wordcraft-cli info $'caf\xe9.docx'
thread 'main' panicked at …/library/std/src/env.rs:878:51:
called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: "caf\xE9.docx"
$ echo $?
101
```

`\xe9` is "é" in Latin-1, as a file copied from an older system or a FAT/ZIP archive can be named.

The calls:

- `apps/wordcraft-cli/src/main.rs:418`: `std::env::args().skip(1).collect()`
- `apps/wordcraft/src/main.rs:242`: `std::env::args().skip(1)`. The app should crash the same way; I didn't launch it to check.

## Expected

No panic. A path argument is opened as the bytes it is (`std::env::args_os()` and `PathBuf`), or the binary prints an error naming the argument and exits non-zero. The never-crash rule in `CLAUDE.md` asks for one of these.

## Related

#1436 and #977 edit the same argument loop in `apps/wordcraft/src/main.rs`. Open PR #1432 adds more `std::env::args()` calls to the app.

title: Markdown import: an unclosed `[` turns every later link in the paragraph into plain text
author: rabis7575
body:
Found while working on #1336.

The Markdown importer caps how far its link and image bracket scans may look ahead in one paragraph (`scan_budget` in `crates/formats/src/markdown.rs`, `tokenize`: 8 × the text length + 8 KB), so hostile input stays linear. But the budget is charged far more than the scans read, so ordinary text runs out of it and every later link in the paragraph is imported as plain text:

1. **A `[` that nothing closes charges the whole budget.** `Intervals [0, 1) and [docs](http://x.org)` imports `[docs](http://x.org)` as text; in CommonMark it is a link.
2. **Every bracket pair charges the rest of the paragraph** (for a link destination it might read), even when no `(` follows the `]`. In a 20 KB paragraph, a dozen references `[1] [2] … [12]` near the start lose a link at its end.
3. **Every link charges the rest of the paragraph too.** In a paragraph with 60 links (about 7.5 KB), only the first 10 stay links.

Expected: a scan costs what it reads, so the budget runs out only on hostile input (as `hostile_importer_input_takes_linear_time` covers), and ordinary links all import.

I'm working on this; a PR will follow.
